description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module withheld the Brazil IEEPA surcharge only from the witness's single aluminum exemplar line (`not entry_is_line_b`) instead of from the whole Section 232 aluminum class that HTS 9903.01.77's carve-out to 9903.85.02 names, so the +40% Brazil duty was over-applied to this chapter's aluminum entries.

Note ch95 is one of the chapters the PR's gate evidence singles out ('9 explained coupling-bound ch95 cells' in G3 and the 2026-08-01 Brazil/forced-labor own-list corrections in G2), i.e. the cells where the witness's own exemplar coupling was the unlawful part -- consistent with this being a genuine behavior change, not a no-op. triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as generalization-only or as a provenance/ceremony change and could not: the diff changes a live formula gate, not metadata, and the module's own proof atom for that term quotes a class-scoped carve-out ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02"), while the pre-fix encoding withheld the Brazil surcharge only when the witness exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` was set. Resolving 9903.85.02 through the pinned release confirms it is a class — "products of aluminum provided for in the tariff headings or subheadings enumerated in subdivision (g) of note 19" — so keying the exception to one exemplar line (or, on the module's other use of that flag, to a metals-exemplar proxy) is a population/scope mismatch with the source in either caller reading, and in a chapter-86 composition it means the carve-out cannot fire for real §232-aluminum entries. The kind holds against its nearest rival, untraceable_branch: the cited provision and the branch itself are unchanged and correctly grounded before and after; only the set of entries the exception applies to was wrong. The second half of the diff (steel parameter re-grounded from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02) is provenance-only and does not carry the verdict — the rate stays '0.50'.

triage.verifier_notes: inferred from verified sibling module index 84 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Scope of the confirmed defect is narrower than the first reader's quote implies. The quote used ("membership-semantic caller inputs ... gain a Section 232 steel component") describes PR #1300 as a whole; for this module those parts landed in the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces"), which already left §122, §232 aluminum/steel and the China-301 slots on membership inputs and already contained `section_232_steel_component_rate`. This commit (198bee703e) is the certify/repair round, and the entire meaning change in ch86.yaml is the two identical Brazil-gate lines (rules `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, versions[0].formula). Everything else in the 58-line diff is the steel proof re-grounding: `source:` string plus proof-atom corpus_citation_path/excerpt, two atoms collapsed into one, value unchanged at '0.50' — mechanical provenance on its own. I verified the "stale locator" claim through the pinned release (corpus us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap): `us/statute/hts/9903.81.87` does not resolve, `us/statute/hts/9903.82.02` resolves to "articles of aluminum, of steel or of copper and derivative aluminum or steel articles, as provided for in subdivisions (c)(i)–(v) of U.S. note 16 ... + 50%". Two caveats for the pruner: (1) the affected version window is effective_from '2026-02-15' / effective_to '2026-02-19', with the next version switching to `terminated_ieepa_additional_ad_valorem_duty_rate` from '2026-02-20', so the mis-scoped carve-out only bites in a five-day window; (2) the generalization is partial — `entry_is_line_b` is still the formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (proof atom 9903.01.33) in the post file, and the PR comment says exemplar flags a/b/d are retained, so this is one gate moved rather than a complete de-exemplarization. I did not verify the "+40%" figure in the first reader's reading: `brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate` is an imported identifier (overlay `us:policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/overlays/ieepa/brazil-9903-01-77`) and its value does not appear in this module. Direction of the error is as the first reader states: `not entry_is_line_b` is true for ordinary entries, so the surcharge was applied where the source exempts it. If a reviewer prefers to score by "the condition had no source basis and was re-grounded," untraceable_branch is a defensible second choice; I rank it lower because the provision cited by the atom is identical pre and post.
